newsitem.title: USA: Cowen cuts AOL Q3 EPS to loss of $0.10/shr.
newsitem.headline: Cowen cuts AOL Q3 EPS to loss of $0.10/shr.

text.p: Cowen & Co analyst Jamie Kiggen said he cut his third quarter estimate on America Online Inc to a loss of $0.10 a share, from break-even previously, due to AOL's cost to lease modems to expand its network.

"It will hit the income statement," Kiggen said, adding that he is allowing for a cost of $15 million for AOL to lease 50,000 modems from other network providers. The move will help AOL upgrade its network capacity two months ahead of schedule.
Kiggen said that AOL's second quarter loss was "right in line" with his expectations and he is still looking to the June quarter for AOL to return to profitability.

Kiggen said that he was pleased by the increased revenues in the non-subscriber areas, such as advertising and electronic commerce, which jumped 50 percent to $40 million on a sequential basis, in the quarter.
"I'm looking for that trendline to improve," Kiggen said, adding that this is where the new financial model for AOL starts to work.
AOL shares were off 1-3/8 to 36-3/4 in active trading.
